rows.name: OLMoTrace
aka: OLMoTrace: Tracing Language Model Outputs Back to Trillions of Training Tokens
rows.operator: Ai2 (The Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence), as a feature in the Ai2 Playground; the paper's authors are Jiacheng Liu and 30 others
rows.kind: a feature in the Ai2 Playground that traces language model outputs back to their full training data in real time; its paper calls it a system, released as open source
rows.unit: a span of a model response that appears verbatim at least once in the model's training data, shown with up to 10 document snippets from that data
rows.record_object: verbatim matches between segments of a language model's output and documents in its training corpora, for Ai2's OLMo models (OLMo 2 32B Instruct, OLMo 2 13B Instruct, OLMoE 1B 7B Instruct) and for any model whose training data is accessible

record.in_layer: it matches output against the model's full training data: for OLMo 2 32B Instruct, five datasets across pretraining, mid-training, supervised finetuning, preference learning and RL, about 3.2 billion documents and 4.6 trillion tokens
record.name: not recorded; the side panel shows document snippets from the training data, and the saved sources do not say whether a document's author, title or source address is shown; Ai2 leaves it to the user to 'personally verify that these documents come from trusted sources'

record.makes: the model's response, of which only long, unique, self-contained spans with a verbatim match are highlighted (K = 0.05 times the response's token count); Ai2 shows it tracing 'creative' expressions, arithmetic and a false knowledge-cutoff claim to training documents, in its own hedged terms ('may have learned', 'could have easily learned it through memorization')

rows.method: infini-gram indexing of the training data and a parallel span-finding algorithm (O(L * log N)); spans meeting existence, self-containment and maximality criteria are ranked by span unigram probability, the lowest K kept, document snippets retrieved and ranked by BM25

self_description.quote: Today we introduce OLMoTrace, a one-of-a-kind feature in the Ai2 Playground that lets you trace the outputs of language models back to their full, multi-trillion-token training data in real time.

operator.quote: © The Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence - All Rights Reserved.

purpose.quote: We developed OLMoTrace to enable researchers, developers, and the general public to inspect where and how language models may have learned to generate certain word sequences.

models.quote: OLMoTrace is available today with our three flagship models: OLMo 2 32B Instruct , OLMo 2 13B Instruct , and OLMoE 1B 7B Instruct , and it can be applied to any language model for which you have access to the training data.

unit.quote: The highlights indicate long and unique spans that appear verbatim at least once in the training data of this model.

partial_cover.quote: Sometimes, a highlighted span may not be present contiguously in any single document, but different parts of that span are present (possibly in different documents) and together they cover the entire span.

limit_nuanced.quote: The interpretation of text matches with training data is quite nuanced.

name_verify.quote: If you personally verify that these documents come from trusted sources, you can gain confidence that this piece of information generated by the model is factually correct.

low_relevance.quote: We use a less saturated color to highlight spans with less relevant documents, and they are labeled in the document list as “low relevance.”

creative.quote: In creative writing tasks there is less of a need for fact checking, but you can still trace certain LM-generated expressions back to the training documents.

memorization.quote: OLMoTrace reveals that this entire expression appears multiple times in the training data, so the model could have easily learned it through memorization.

cutoff_case.quote: now we can see that the model may have learned to say August 2023 from the post-training examples listed on the right.

period.quote: since its pre-training data has a cutoff of December 2022

limit_early.quote: We are still in an early stage in exploring the full potential of this tool

criteria.quote: Maximality : The span is not a subspan of another span that meets the above two criteria.

method_index.quote: To speed up computation, we index the training data with infini-gram and develop a novel parallel algorithm, reducing the time complexity of span finding from the naive O(L^2 * N) to O(L * log N)

method_k.quote: keeps the K spans with the smallest unigram probability, where K = 0.05 * the number of tokens in the model output.

snippets.quote: For each kept span, OLMoTrace retrieves up to 10 document snippets enclosing this span from the training data, which are displayed in the side panel. If there are more than 10 documents for a span, a random set of 10 is sampled.

bm25.quote: in the document panel we rank all documents by a BM25 score in descending order.

count.quote: In total, these five datasets contain about 3.2 billion documents and 4.6 trillion tokens, and OLMoTrace matches against all of them.

code.quote: We also release our source code .

paper_abstract.quote: OLMoTrace finds and shows verbatim matches between segments of language model output and documents in the training text corpora.

speed.quote: our system returns tracing results within a few seconds.

creativity.quote: We showcase how it can be used to explore fact checking, hallucination, and the creativity of language models.

license.quote: OLMoTrace is publicly available and fully open-source.

authors.quote: by Jiacheng Liu and 30 other authors
